title: Shane Black Xmas Thrillers on either side of the Ironic Meta Divide

commenti.body:
> Backstory: Shane had passed out headfirst into a large bowl of Christmas punch while watching Die Hard one Christmas Eve, and as he transitioned to the other side he had a prophetic vision that one day he would become a great man in Hollywood, if he made all action thrillers snarky comedies set during Christmas, and if he stayed away from reboots of established space-monster horror franchises. He awoke from his drowning stupor and decided to follow his vision. He would subsequently have great success following the 'Die Hard Protocol'

Surely he deserves a little more credit than this. Before 1995, Shane Black had already written Lethal Weapon, The Last Boy Scout, and The Last Action Hero. To the degree that he's some kind of copyist, he sort of made the mold himself, didn't he?
He had teachers and very respectful to his mentors like Walter Hill. What he was taught I believe was to have a distinct, creative voice. His body of work is monumental.
It's just meant as a bit of fun, I'm not seriously saying he copied anything. Throughout the essay I'm poking some fun at him in the same snarky spirit he likes to use himself.
